title: The Reflexivity Threshold: A Phase Transition for Multi-Agent Performative Prediction
title_zh: 反身性阈值：多智能体执行性预测的相变

paragraphs.en: Many learning systems are performative: once deployed, their predictions change the data distribution on which future models are trained. In multi-agent settings, this feedback is routed through a network of interacting learners, so stability depends not only on the strength of performativity but also on who affects whom. We study repeated retraining in multi-agent performative prediction and identify a spectral threshold that separates stable learning from worst-case learning obstruction. Prior work often collapses cross-agent feedback into a scalar contraction constant, missing this network structure. We instead introduce the reflexivity matrix Γ \Gamma , which records how strongly one agent’s deployment can move another agent’s best response, defined from per-agent gradient sensitivities and curvature parameters. The threshold occurs when the spectral radius of this matrix crosses one. Below the threshold, repeated retraining converges geometrically to a unique performatively stable equilibrium, with cumulative excess loss bounded uniformly in the time horizon. Above the threshold, we construct noisy supercritical instances in which every local-information learner incurs expected cumulative excess loss growing linearly for horizons up to order 1 / ( ρ ⁡ ( Γ ) − 1 ) 1/(\rho(\Gamma)-1) . Together, these results characterize the threshold behavior through upper and lower bounds and recover the single-agent scalar threshold from prior work as a special case.

paragraphs.en: Many learning systems, once deployed, change the environment that later generates their training data. A credit scoring model can change how applicants behave; an algorithmic trading strategy can move the price data on which future strategies are trained. This feedback effect is the focus of performative prediction. Existing theory largely studies the case of one learner facing the consequences of its own deployment. Many real systems, however, contain multiple learners whose deployments jointly shape the environment.
paragraphs.zh: 许多学习系统在部署之后，会改变随后生成其训练数据的环境。 信用评分模型可能改变申请人的行为；算法交易策略可能影响未来策略训练所依据的价格数据。 这种反馈效应正是执行性预测的研究焦点。 现有理论主要研究的是单个智能体面对自身部署后果的情形。 然而，许多真实系统包含多个智能体，它们的部署共同塑造了环境。

paragraphs.en: The multi-agent setting is not simply a larger version of the single-agent problem; it introduces different difficulties. Feedback can travel across agents: one agent’s deployment changes the data distribution, which changes another agent’s retraining problem, which may itself affect the data distribution or other agents. Stability therefore depends not only on the overall strength of performativity, but also on how feedback is routed through the agent network.
paragraphs.zh: 多智能体环境并不是单智能体问题的一个简单放大版本；它带来了不同的困难。 反馈可以在智能体之间传递：一个智能体的部署改变了数据分布，这又改变了另一个智能体的再训练问题，而后者本身可能进一步影响数据分布或其他智能体。 因此，稳定性不仅取决于执行性的总体强度，还取决于反馈在智能体网络中的传递路径。

paragraphs.en: This paper draws on three lines of research. The first is the single-agent theory of performative prediction, which introduces the framework we extend. The second is the multi-agent theory of performative prediction and decision-dependent games, which is where our contribution is most directly positioned. The third is the combined tradition of spectral methods for network games and statistical lower bound techniques, from which we import two standard technical tools.

(2020) introduced performative prediction in a single-agent setting, formalizing performative stability and convergence of repeated retraining under sensitivity conditions. Subsequent work largely retained this single-agent viewpoint while extending the framework to stochastic, causal, nonconvex, and sequential settings ( Mendler-Dünner et al., 2020 ; Miller et al., 2021 ; Brown et al., 2022 ; Hardt et al., 2022 ; Mofakhami et al., 2023 ; Mandal et al., 2023 ) . Closest to our threshold result, Anagnostides et al. (2026) established hardness and lower bounds at the single-agent scalar threshold. We depart from this line by studying decentralized multi-agent retraining, where performative feedback is cross-agent and the scalar threshold is replaced by the spectral condition ρ ⁡ ( Γ ) = 1 \rho(\Gamma)=1 .

paragraphs.en: The third identifies dynamical phase transitions. Piliouras and Yu (2023) proved a transition from stability to Li–Yorke chaos as update aggressiveness grows under scalar aggregate influence. Their threshold is dynamical and concerns the long-run behavior of specific update rules; ours is information-theoretic and applies to every decentralized local-information learner. Farina and Perdomo (2026) show that, for bounded losses, no-regret online learning yields approximate performative stability of a mixture over joint deployment histories, without regularity assumptions on the distribution maps. Our subcritical result guarantees geometric convergence of the last retraining iterate to a unique performatively stable equilibrium under curvature and sensitivity assumptions.

paragraphs.en: Two technical traditions supply tools used in our analysis without serving as competing frameworks. Spectral conditions for equilibrium uniqueness and stability are well established in network games ( Ballester et al., 2006 ; Bramoullé et al., 2014 ; Parise and Ozdaglar, 2019 ) , where the spectral radius governs payoff coupling: agent j j ’s action enters agent i i ’s utility directly. In our setting, it governs distributional feedback through D ⁡ ( w ) D(w) , and Γ \Gamma is built from gradient sensitivities and curvature constants rather than payoff coefficients. Our lower bound uses the two-point method ( Tsybakov, 2009 ) ; recent extensions to interactive ( Chen et al., 2024 ) and decision-dependent ( Cutler et al., 2024 ) settings do not cover our performative learning setting. Our construction is tailored to multi-agent performative feedback over a finite horizon.
paragraphs.zh: 两个技术传统为我们分析中所使用的工具提供了来源，但并不构成相互竞争的框架。 关于均衡唯一性与稳定性的谱条件在网络博弈中已有充分研究（Ballester 等，2006；Bramoullé 等，2014；Parise 和 Ozdaglar，2019），其中谱半径刻画收益耦合：智能体 j 的行为直接进入智能体 i 的效用。 在我们的设定中，谱半径通过 D(w) 刻画分布反馈，而 Γ 由梯度敏感度与曲率常数构成，而非收益系数。 我们的下界采用两点法（Tsybakov，2009）；近期针对交互式（Chen 等，2024）与决策依赖（Cutler 等，2024）设定的扩展并不涵盖我们的策略性学习设定。 我们的构造专为有限时域上的多智能体策略性反馈而设计。

paragraphs.en: Section 5 established that ρ ⁡ ( Γ ) < 1 \rho(\Gamma)<1 is sufficient for geometric convergence and bounded cumulative excess loss. Whether the supercritical regime produces an intrinsic learning obstruction is delicate: failure of contraction does not by itself imply information-theoretic impossibility, since with enough observations a learner may recover the correct equilibrium even when repeated retraining diverges. We show that the threshold has a sharp negative side in the worst case. For every ε > 0 \varepsilon>0 , we construct a supercritical family with ρ ⁡ ( Γ ) = 1 + ε \rho(\Gamma)=1+\varepsilon in which any decentralized local-information learner—one that at each round uses only its own history of observations and actions—incurs linear cumulative excess loss for T = O ⁡ ( 1 / ε ) T=O(1/\varepsilon) rounds.
paragraphs.zh: 第 5 节已确立 ρ ⁡ ( Γ ) < 1 \rho(\Gamma)<1 是几何收敛与有界累计超额损失的充分条件。 超临界情形是否会产生内在的学习障碍是一个微妙的问题：收缩性的失效本身并不意味着信息论上的不可能，因为只要观测足够多，学习者即使面临反复再训练发散的情况，仍可能恢复正确的均衡。 我们证明该阈值在最坏情形下具有陡峭的负面一侧。 对每个 ε > 0 \varepsilon>0 ，我们构造一个满足 ρ ⁡ ( Γ ) = 1 + ε \rho(\Gamma)=1+\varepsilon 的超临界族，其中任何去中心化的局部信息智能体——即每一轮仅使用自身观测与动作历史的智能体——在 T = O ⁡ ( 1 / ε ) T=O(1/\varepsilon) 轮内都会产生线性累计超额损失。

paragraphs.en: The framework replaces a scalar Lipschitz constant with the reflexivity matrix Γ \Gamma , whose entries a i ​ j / μ i a_{ij}/\mu_{i} retain the per-pair structure of performative feedback. This matters because two systems with the same scalar bound can have different stability behavior if their feedback is routed through different agent networks. The Perron weights q q in Theorem 4 encode this heterogeneity by rescaling agents according to their role in the collective retraining dynamics. When k = 1 k=1 , Γ \Gamma reduces to the scalar ratio a 11 / μ 1 a_{11}/\mu_{1} , recovering the single-agent contraction threshold of Perdomo et al. (2020) . More generally, ρ ⁡ ( Γ ) = 1 \rho(\Gamma)=1 separates dissipative feedback, where repeated retraining contracts, from supercritical feedback, where uniform stability guarantees fail. We use reflexivity for this deployment-to-data channel, following the financial-market terminology of Soros (1987) ; we do not formalize the broader economic concept.

paragraphs.en: Several modeling choices delimit our results. The main guarantees assume strong convexity in each agent’s own action and exact best-response retraining; Appendix C controls approximate retraining under explicit error bounds. paragraphs.en: It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.
paragraphs.zh: 只要明确这些目标并非论文已经实现的目标，那么将愿景式的目标作为动机写进来是可以接受的。

paragraphs.en: Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：论文是否讨论了作者所开展工作的局限性？

paragraphs.en: Justification: The paper discusses limitations in Section 7.
paragraphs.zh: 理由：论文在第 7 节中讨论了局限性。

paragraphs.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper.
paragraphs.zh: 回答 [N/A] 表示该论文没有局限性，而回答 [No] 表示该论文存在局限性，但论文中未对此进行讨论。

paragraphs.en: The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper.
paragraphs.zh: 鼓励作者在论文中单独创建一节「Limitations（局限性）」。

paragraphs.en: The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be.
paragraphs.zh: 论文应指出任何较强的假设，以及结果对这些假设被违反时的稳健性如何（例如，独立性假设、无噪声环境、模型设定正确、仅在局部成立的渐近近似）。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何被违反，以及由此带来的影响是什么。

sents.en: The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally).
sents.zh: 论文应指出任何较强的假设，以及结果对这些假设被违反时的稳健性如何（例如，独立性假设、无噪声环境、模型设定正确、仅在局部成立的渐近近似）。

sents.en: The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be.
sents.zh: 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何被违反，以及由此带来的影响是什么。

paragraphs.en: The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated.
paragraphs.zh: 作者应当反思所做声明的适用范围，例如，如果该方法仅在少数数据集上或仅进行了少数几次运行测试。 总的来说，实证结果往往依赖于隐含的假设，而这些假设应当被明确阐述。

sents.en: The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs.
sents.zh: 作者应当反思所做声明的适用范围，例如，如果该方法仅在少数数据集上或仅进行了少数几次运行测试。

sents.en: In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated.
sents.zh: 总的来说，实证结果往往依赖于隐含的假设，而这些假设应当被明确阐述。

paragraphs.en: The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon.
paragraphs.zh: 作者应当反思影响该方法性能的因素。 例如，人脸识别算法在图像分辨率较低或拍摄于弱光环境下时，可能表现不佳。 或者，语音转文字系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线课程提供隐藏式字幕，因为它无法处理专业术语。

sents.en: The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach.
sents.zh: 作者应当反思影响该方法性能的因素。

sents.en: For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting.
sents.zh: 例如，人脸识别算法在图像分辨率较低或拍摄于弱光环境下时，可能表现不佳。

sents.en: Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon.
sents.zh: 或者，语音转文字系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线课程提供隐藏式字幕，因为它无法处理专业术语。

paragraphs.en: The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size.
paragraphs.zh: 作者应当讨论所提出算法的计算效率，以及它们如何随数据集规模进行扩展。

paragraphs.en: If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness.
paragraphs.zh: 如适用，作者应讨论其方法在解决隐私和公平性问题方面可能存在的局限性。

paragraphs.en: While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管作者可能担心对局限性完全坦诚会被审稿人用作拒稿的理由，但更糟糕的结果可能是审稿人发现了论文中未曾承认的局限性。 作者应当运用自己的最佳判断，并认识到支持透明度的个人行为在发展维护社区诚信的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 审稿人将被明确指示不要因对局限性的坦诚而给予负面评价。

sents.en: While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper.
sents.zh: 尽管作者可能担心对局限性完全坦诚会被审稿人用作拒稿的理由，但更糟糕的结果可能是审稿人发现了论文中未曾承认的局限性。

sents.en: The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community.
sents.zh: 作者应当运用自己的最佳判断，并认识到支持透明度的个人行为在发展维护社区诚信的规范方面发挥着重要作用。

sents.en: Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.
sents.zh: 审稿人将被明确指示不要因对局限性的坦诚而给予负面评价。

paragraphs.en: Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：对于每个理论结果，论文是否提供了完整的假设集合以及完整（且正确）的证明？

paragraphs.en: Justification: The theoretical results state their assumptions explicitly, including strong convexity, gradient sensitivity, unconstrained domains, smoothness, and the decentralized information model. Proofs are provided in the main text for the subcritical results, and the full proof of the lower bound is provided in Appendix A.
paragraphs.zh: 理由：理论结果明确陈述了其假设条件，包括强凸性、梯度敏感性、无约束域、光滑性以及去中心化信息模型。 次临界结果的证明在正文中给出，下界的完整证明见附录 A。

sents.en: Justification: The theoretical results state their assumptions explicitly, including strong convexity, gradient sensitivity, unconstrained domains, smoothness, and the decentralized information model.
sents.zh: 理由：理论结果明确陈述了其假设条件，包括强凸性、梯度敏感性、无约束域、光滑性以及去中心化信息模型。

sents.en: Proofs are provided in the main text for the subcritical results, and the full proof of the lower bound is provided in Appendix A.
sents.zh: 次临界结果的证明在正文中给出，下界的完整证明见附录 A。

paragraphs.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results.
paragraphs.zh: 答案 [N/A] 表示该论文不包含理论结果。

paragraphs.en: All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced.
paragraphs.zh: 论文中所有的定理、公式和证明都应编号并进行交叉引用。

paragraphs.en: All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems.
paragraphs.zh: 所有假设均应在任何定理的陈述中明确说明或引用。

paragraphs.en: The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition.
paragraphs.zh: 证明可以出现在正文或补充材料中，但如果出现在补充材料中，鼓励作者提供简短的证明概要以提供直观理解。

paragraphs.en: Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material.
paragraphs.zh: 反之，论文正文中的任何非正式证明都应由附录或补充材料中提供的正式证明加以补充。

paragraphs.en: Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced.
paragraphs.zh: 证明所依赖的定理和引理应当被适当地引用。

paragraphs.en: Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：论文是否充分披露了复现论文主要实验结果所需的全部信息，以至于影响论文的主要论断和/或结论（无论是否提供代码和数据）？

paragraphs.en: Justification: The simulation setup details are described in Appendix B . The simulation code, seeds, dependencies, and reproduction commands are provided in the supplementary material.
paragraphs.zh: 理由：仿真设置的详细信息见附录 B。 仿真代码、随机种子、依赖项以及复现命令已在补充材料中提供。

sents.en: Justification: The simulation setup details are described in Appendix B .
sents.zh: 理由：仿真设置的详细信息见附录 B。

sents.en: The simulation code, seeds, dependencies, and reproduction commands are provided in the supplementary material.
sents.zh: 仿真代码、随机种子、依赖项以及复现命令已在补充材料中提供。

paragraphs.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments.
paragraphs.zh: 答案 [N/A] 表示该论文不包含实验。

paragraphs.en: If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not.
paragraphs.zh: 如果论文包含实验，审稿人对该问题回答 [No] 的印象会不佳：无论是否提供代码和数据，使论文具备可复现性都很重要。

paragraphs.en: If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable.
paragraphs.zh: 如果贡献是数据集和/或模型，作者应描述其为使结果可复现或可验证所采取的步骤。

paragraphs.en: Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed.
paragraphs.zh: 根据贡献的不同，可复现性可以通过多种方式来实现。 例如，如果贡献是一种新的架构，那么完整地描述该架构可能就足够了；而如果贡献是一个具体的模型及其经验评估，则可能需要让他人能够使用相同的数据集复现该模型，或者提供对该模型的访问。 一般来说，发布代码和数据通常是实现这一目标的一种好方法，但可复现性也可以通过提供如何复现结果的详细说明、提供托管模型的访问权限（例如，在大语言模型的情况下）、发布模型检查点，或以适合所做研究的其他方式来保障。

sents.en: Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways.
sents.zh: 根据贡献的不同，可复现性可以通过多种方式来实现。

sents.en: For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model.
sents.zh: 例如，如果贡献是一种新的架构，那么完整地描述该架构可能就足够了；而如果贡献是一个具体的模型及其经验评估，则可能需要让他人能够使用相同的数据集复现该模型，或者提供对该模型的访问。

sents.en: In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed.
sents.zh: 一般来说，发布代码和数据通常是实现这一目标的一种好方法，但可复现性也可以通过提供如何复现结果的详细说明、提供托管模型的访问权限（例如，在大语言模型的情况下）、发布模型检查点，或以适合所做研究的其他方式来保障。

paragraphs.en: While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example
paragraphs.zh: 虽然 NeurIPS 不要求公开代码，但会议确实要求所有投稿提供某种合理的可复现性途径，这可能取决于贡献的性质。例如

paragraphs.en: If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm.
paragraphs.zh: 如果贡献主要是一种新算法，论文应当清楚地说明如何复现该算法。

paragraphs.en: If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully.
paragraphs.zh: 如果贡献主要是一种新的模型架构，论文应清晰且完整地描述该架构。

paragraphs.en: If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset).
paragraphs.zh: 如果贡献是一个新模型（例如，一个大语言模型），则应当提供一种访问该模型以复现结果的方式，或者提供一种复现该模型的方式（例如，使用开源数据集或关于如何构建该数据集的说明）。

paragraphs.en: We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.
paragraphs.zh: 我们认识到，在某些情况下可复现性可能比较棘手，此时欢迎作者描述他们为保障可复现性而提供的特定方式。 对于闭源模型，对模型的访问可能在某种程度上受到限制（例如仅限注册用户），但其他研究者仍应有可能通过某种途径来复现或验证这些结果。

sents.en: We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility.
sents.zh: 我们认识到，在某些情况下可复现性可能比较棘手，此时欢迎作者描述他们为保障可复现性而提供的特定方式。

sents.en: In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.
sents.zh: 对于闭源模型，对模型的访问可能在某种程度上受到限制（例如仅限注册用户），但其他研究者仍应有可能通过某种途径来复现或验证这些结果。

paragraphs.en: Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：论文是否提供了数据和代码的开放获取，并附带足够的说明以忠实地复现补充材料中描述的主要实验结果？

paragraphs.en: Justification: The simulations use synthetic matrices and do not rely on external datasets. The supplementary material includes the simulation code, seeds, dependencies, and instructions to reproduce Figure 1 .
paragraphs.zh: 理由：仿真使用合成矩阵，不依赖外部数据集。 补充材料包含仿真代码、随机种子、依赖项以及复现图 1 的说明。

sents.en: Justification: The simulations use synthetic matrices and do not rely on external datasets.
sents.zh: 理由：仿真使用合成矩阵，不依赖外部数据集。

sents.en: The supplementary material includes the simulation code, seeds, dependencies, and instructions to reproduce Figure 1 .
sents.zh: 补充材料包含仿真代码、随机种子、依赖项以及复现图 1 的说明。

paragraphs.en: The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code.
paragraphs.zh: 答案 [N/A] 表示该论文不包含需要代码的实验。

paragraphs.en: Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details.
paragraphs.zh: 请参阅 NeurIPS 代码与数据提交指南（ https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ）以了解更多详细信息。

paragraphs.en: While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark).
paragraphs.zh: 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据，但我们理解这有时可能无法实现，因此回答「否」是可以接受的。 论文不能仅因为没有包含代码而被拒绝，除非代码是该贡献的核心（例如，对于一个新的开源基准测试）。

sents.en: While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer.
sents.zh: 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据，但我们理解这有时可能无法实现，因此回答「否」是可以接受的。

sents.en: Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark).
sents.zh: 论文不能仅因为没有包含代码而被拒绝，除非代码是该贡献的核心（例如，对于一个新的开源基准测试）。

paragraphs.en: The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details.
paragraphs.zh: 说明中应包含复现结果所需运行的确切命令和环境。 更多详情请参阅 NeurIPS 代码与数据提交指南（ https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ）。

sents.en: The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results.
sents.zh: 说明中应包含复现结果所需运行的确切命令和环境。

sents.en: See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details.
sents.zh: 更多详情请参阅 NeurIPS 代码与数据提交指南（ https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ）。

paragraphs.en: The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc.
paragraphs.zh: 作者应提供关于数据访问与准备的说明，包括如何访问原始数据、预处理数据、中间数据和生成数据等。

paragraphs.en: The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why.
paragraphs.zh: 作者应提供脚本，用于复现新提出方法和基线的所有实验结果。 如果只有部分实验可复现，作者应说明哪些实验未包含在脚本中以及原因。

sents.en: The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines.
sents.zh: 作者应提供脚本，用于复现新提出方法和基线的所有实验结果。

sents.en: If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why.
sents.zh: 如果只有部分实验可复现，作者应说明哪些实验未包含在脚本中以及原因。

paragraphs.en: At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable).
paragraphs.zh: 提交时，为保持匿名，作者应发布匿名版本（如适用）。

paragraphs.en: Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted.
paragraphs.zh: 建议在补充材料（附于论文之后）中尽可能多地提供信息，但允许包含数据和代码的 URL 链接。

paragraphs.en: Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：论文是否说明了理解结果所需的全部训练和测试细节（例如：数据划分、超参数及其选择方式、优化器类型）？

paragraphs.en: Justification: Details needed to understand the results of the simulations are given in the main text. Appendix B specifies the full details for Figure 1. The code is also provided.
paragraphs.zh: 理由：理解仿真结果所需的细节已在正文中给出。 附录 B 详细说明了图 1 的全部细节。 同时也提供了代码。

sents.en: Justification: Details needed to understand the results of the simulations are given in the main text.
sents.zh: 理由：理解仿真结果所需的细节已在正文中给出。

sents.en: Appendix B specifies the full details for Figure 1.
sents.zh: 附录 B 详细说明了图 1 的全部细节。

sents.en: The code is also provided.
sents.zh: 同时也提供了代码。

paragraphs.en: The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them.
paragraphs.zh: 实验设置应在论文正文中呈现，详细程度需足以使读者理解结果并领会其意义。

paragraphs.en: The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material.
paragraphs.zh: 完整细节可以通过随代码提供、放在附录中，或作为补充材料的方式给出。

paragraphs.en: Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：论文是否恰当地报告了误差条（error bars）并给出了正确定义，或提供了有关实验统计显著性的其他适当信息？

paragraphs.en: Justification: Panel 1(a) reports medians with interquartile bands across base matrices and initializations. Panel 1(b) reports mean log-distances with pointwise interquartile bands across the draws described in Appendix B .
paragraphs.zh: 理由说明：图 1(a) 报告了不同基矩阵与初始化下的中位数及四分位距带。 图 1(b) 报告了附录 B 中所述各次抽样下的平均对数距离及逐点四分位距带。

sents.en: Justification: Panel 1(a) reports medians with interquartile bands across base matrices and initializations.
sents.zh: 理由说明：图 1(a) 报告了不同基矩阵与初始化下的中位数及四分位距带。

sents.en: Panel 1(b) reports mean log-distances with pointwise interquartile bands across the draws described in Appendix B .
sents.zh: 图 1(b) 报告了附录 B 中所述各次抽样下的平均对数距离及逐点四分位距带。

paragraphs.en: The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper.
paragraphs.zh: 如果结果附有误差条、置信区间或统计显著性检验，作者应回答 [Yes]，至少对于支持论文主要结论的实验应如此。

paragraphs.en: The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions).
paragraphs.zh: 误差棒所捕捉到的变异因素应予以明确说明（例如，训练/测试集划分、初始化、某个参数的随机抽取，或在给定实验条件下的整体运行）。

paragraphs.en: The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.)
paragraphs.zh: 误差棒的计算方法应当予以说明（解析公式、调用库函数、自助法等）。

paragraphs.en: The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors).
paragraphs.zh: 应给出所做的假设（例如，误差服从正态分布）。

paragraphs.en: It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean.
paragraphs.zh: 应明确说明误差线是标准差还是平均值的标准误。

paragraphs.en: It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified.
paragraphs.zh: 可以报告1倍标准差（1-sigma）的误差棒，但应当予以说明。 如果误差服从正态分布的假设未得到验证，作者最好报告2倍标准差（2-sigma）的误差棒，而不是声称自己有96%的置信区间。

sents.en: It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it.
sents.zh: 可以报告1倍标准差（1-sigma）的误差棒，但应当予以说明。

sents.en: The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified.
sents.zh: 如果误差服从正态分布的假设未得到验证，作者最好报告2倍标准差（2-sigma）的误差棒，而不是声称自己有96%的置信区间。

paragraphs.en: For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates).
paragraphs.zh: 对于非对称分布，作者应当小心，不要在表格或图中展示会导致结果超出合理范围（例如，负的错误率）的对称误差棒。

paragraphs.en: If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.
paragraphs.zh: 如果表格或图表中报告了误差线，作者应在文本中解释其计算方式，并在正文中引用相应的图表。

paragraphs.en: Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：对于每个实验，论文是否提供了足够的关于复现实验所需计算机资源（算力工作节点的类型、内存、执行时间）的信息？

paragraphs.en: Justification: The paper does not currently report compute resources for the simulations. Since the experiments are synthetic simulations rather than large-scale training runs, they can be reproduced with standard CPU resources; this is stated in Appendix B.
paragraphs.zh: 理由：论文目前未报告仿真所需的计算资源。 由于实验是合成仿真而非大规模训练运行，使用标准 CPU 资源即可复现；这一点在附录 B 中已有说明。

sents.en: Justification: The paper does not currently report compute resources for the simulations.
sents.zh: 理由：论文目前未报告仿真所需的计算资源。

sents.en: Since the experiments are synthetic simulations rather than large-scale training runs, they can be reproduced with standard CPU resources; this is stated in Appendix B.
sents.zh: 由于实验是合成仿真而非大规模训练运行，使用标准 CPU 资源即可复现；这一点在附录 B 中已有说明。

paragraphs.en: The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage.
paragraphs.zh: 论文应说明计算工作节点的类型（CPU 或 GPU）、内部集群或云服务提供商，包括相关的内存和存储信息。

paragraphs.en: The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute.
paragraphs.zh: 论文应提供每个单独实验运行所需的计算量，并估算总计算量。

paragraphs.en: The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper).
paragraphs.zh: 论文应说明完整的研究项目是否需要比论文中报告的实验更多的计算资源（例如，未写入论文的初步实验或失败实验）。

paragraphs.en: Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：论文中所开展的研究是否在各方面都符合 NeurIPS 伦理准则 https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ？

paragraphs.en: Justification: The work is theoretical and uses synthetic simulations only. It does not involve human subjects, private data, scraped data, deployed systems, or high-risk model release, and the authors have reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics.
paragraphs.zh: 理由：这项工作是理论性的，仅使用了合成模拟。 它不涉及人类受试者、私人数据、抓取的数据、部署的系统或高风险模型发布，且作者已审阅 NeurIPS 伦理准则。

sents.en: Justification: The work is theoretical and uses synthetic simulations only.
sents.zh: 理由：这项工作是理论性的，仅使用了合成模拟。

sents.en: It does not involve human subjects, private data, scraped data, deployed systems, or high-risk model release, and the authors have reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics.
sents.zh: 它不涉及人类受试者、私人数据、抓取的数据、部署的系统或高风险模型发布，且作者已审阅 NeurIPS 伦理准则。

paragraphs.en: The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics.
paragraphs.zh: 回答 [N/A] 表示作者尚未审阅 NeurIPS 伦理准则。

paragraphs.en: If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics.
paragraphs.zh: 如果作者回答 [否]，则应说明需要偏离《伦理准则》的特殊情况。

paragraphs.en: The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction).
paragraphs.zh: 作者应确保保持匿名性（例如，如果其所在司法辖区的法律或法规有特殊考量）。

paragraphs.en: Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：论文是否讨论了所做工作可能带来的积极社会影响和消极社会影响？

paragraphs.en: Justification: The paper is foundational and is not tied to a deployed system. We do not identify a clear direct path to negative applications, and the paper does not include a dedicated discussion of positive and negative societal impacts.
paragraphs.zh: 理由：该论文是基础性研究，并未与任何已部署的系统相关联。 我们没有发现通向负面应用的明确直接路径，且论文中未包含关于正面与负面社会影响的专门讨论。

sents.en: Justification: The paper is foundational and is not tied to a deployed system.
sents.zh: 理由：该论文是基础性研究，并未与任何已部署的系统相关联。

sents.en: We do not identify a clear direct path to negative applications, and the paper does not include a dedicated discussion of positive and negative societal impacts.
sents.zh: 我们没有发现通向负面应用的明确直接路径，且论文中未包含关于正面与负面社会影响的专门讨论。

paragraphs.en: The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed.
paragraphs.zh: 答案 [N/A] 表示所开展的工作不存在社会影响。

paragraphs.en: If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact.
paragraphs.zh: 如果作者回答 [N/A] 或 [No]，则应解释为什么其工作没有社会影响，或者为什么论文未涉及社会影响。

paragraphs.en: Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations.
paragraphs.zh: 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或非预期用途（例如，虚假信息、生成虚假个人资料、监控）、公平性考量（例如，部署可能做出对特定群体造成不公平影响决策的技术）、隐私考量以及安全考量。

paragraphs.en: The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster.
paragraphs.zh: 会议预计许多论文将属于基础研究，并不与特定应用挂钩，更不用说部署了。 然而，如果存在通往任何负面应用的直接路径，作者应当指出这一点。 例如，指出生成模型质量的提升可能被用于生成虚假信息的深度伪造（Deepfakes），是合理的。 另一方面，没有必要指出用于优化神经网络的通用算法可能使人们能够更快地训练出生成深度伪造的模型。

sents.en: The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments.
sents.zh: 会议预计许多论文将属于基础研究，并不与特定应用挂钩，更不用说部署了。

sents.en: However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out.
sents.zh: 然而，如果存在通往任何负面应用的直接路径，作者应当指出这一点。

sents.en: For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation.
sents.zh: 例如，指出生成模型质量的提升可能被用于生成虚假信息的深度伪造（Deepfakes），是合理的。

sents.en: On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster.
sents.zh: 另一方面，没有必要指出用于优化神经网络的通用算法可能使人们能够更快地训练出生成深度伪造的模型。

paragraphs.en: The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology.
paragraphs.zh: 作者应当考虑以下几类可能的危害：技术在被按预期使用且正常运行时可能产生的危害；技术在被按预期使用但给出错误结果时可能产生的危害；以及因（有意或无意的）滥用技术而产生的危害。

paragraphs.en: If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML).
paragraphs.zh: 如果存在负面的社会影响，作者还可以讨论可能的缓解策略（例如，模型的受控发布、在提供攻击的同时提供防御、监测滥用行为的机制、监控系统如何随时间从反馈中学习的机制、提高机器学习的效率和可及性）。

paragraphs.en: Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：论文是否描述了针对负责任地发布具有较高误用风险的数据或模型（例如，预训练语言模型、图像生成器或抓取的数据集）所采取的保障措施？

paragraphs.en: Justification: The paper does not release artifacts with substantial misuse risk. The only released artifacts are synthetic simulation code.
paragraphs.zh: 理由：该论文未发布具有较大误用风险的产出物。 唯一发布的产出物是合成仿真代码。

sents.en: Justification: The paper does not release artifacts with substantial misuse risk.
sents.zh: 理由：该论文未发布具有较大误用风险的产出物。

sents.en: The only released artifacts are synthetic simulation code.
sents.zh: 唯一发布的产出物是合成仿真代码。

paragraphs.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks.
paragraphs.zh: 答案 [N/A] 表示该论文不存在此类风险。

paragraphs.en: Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters.
paragraphs.zh: 具有较高滥用或双用途风险的已发布模型，应当在发布时配备必要的防护措施，以实现对模型的可控使用，例如要求用户遵守使用指南或访问限制，或实施安全过滤器。

paragraphs.en: Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images.
paragraphs.zh: 从互联网上抓取的数据集可能带来安全风险。 作者应说明他们如何避免发布不安全的图像。

sents.en: Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks.
sents.zh: 从互联网上抓取的数据集可能带来安全风险。

sents.en: The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images.
sents.zh: 作者应说明他们如何避免发布不安全的图像。

paragraphs.en: We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort.
paragraphs.zh: 我们认识到，提供有效的保障措施具有挑战性，而且许多论文并不要求这样做，但我们鼓励作者将这一点考虑在内，并尽最大努力去做。

paragraphs.en: Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：论文中使用的资产（例如代码、数据、模型）的创作者或原始所有者是否得到了恰当的署名，并且是否明确提及并恰当遵守了许可证和使用条款？

paragraphs.en: Justification: The paper does not use existing datasets, pretrained models, or third-party code assets as part of the research contribution. The work is theoretical and uses synthetic simulations.
paragraphs.zh: 理由说明：本文没有将现有数据集、预训练模型或第三方代码资产作为研究贡献的一部分。 该工作是理论性的，并使用合成模拟。

sents.en: Justification: The paper does not use existing datasets, pretrained models, or third-party code assets as part of the research contribution.
sents.zh: 理由说明：本文没有将现有数据集、预训练模型或第三方代码资产作为研究贡献的一部分。

sents.en: The work is theoretical and uses synthetic simulations.
sents.zh: 该工作是理论性的，并使用合成模拟。

paragraphs.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets.
paragraphs.zh: 答案 [N/A] 表示该论文没有使用现有资产。

paragraphs.en: The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset.
paragraphs.zh: 作者应当引用产生该代码包或数据集的原始论文。

paragraphs.en: The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL.
paragraphs.zh: 作者应说明所使用的是该资源的哪个版本，并尽可能提供一个 URL。

paragraphs.en: The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset.
paragraphs.zh: 每个资产都应注明许可证名称（例如 CC-BY 4.0）。

paragraphs.en: For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided.
paragraphs.zh: 对于从特定来源（例如网站）抓取的数据，应提供该来源的版权和服务条款。

paragraphs.en: If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset.
paragraphs.zh: 如果发布了资产，应提供数据包中的许可证、版权信息和使用条款。 对于热门数据集，paperswithcode.com/datasets 已为部分数据集整理了许可证信息。 该网站的许可指南可以帮助确定数据集的许可证。

sents.en: If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided.
sents.zh: 如果发布了资产，应提供数据包中的许可证、版权信息和使用条款。

sents.en: For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets.
sents.zh: 对于热门数据集，paperswithcode.com/datasets 已为部分数据集整理了许可证信息。

sents.en: Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset.
sents.zh: 该网站的许可指南可以帮助确定数据集的许可证。

paragraphs.en: For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided.
paragraphs.zh: 对于重新打包的现有数据集，应同时提供原始许可证和衍生资产许可证（如有变更）。

paragraphs.en: If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators.
paragraphs.zh: 如果这些信息无法在网上获取，建议作者联系该资产的创作者。

paragraphs.en: Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：论文中引入的新资产是否有完善的文档记录，并且文档是否随资产一并提供？

paragraphs.en: Justification: The paper releases synthetic simulation code and seeds. These assets are accompanied by documentation describing the simulation procedure, dependencies, commands needed to reproduce the figures, and an appropriate license.
paragraphs.zh: 理由说明：论文发布了合成仿真代码和随机种子。 这些资产附带文档，描述了仿真流程、依赖项、复现图表所需的命令，以及合适的许可证。

sents.en: Justification: The paper releases synthetic simulation code and seeds.
sents.zh: 理由说明：论文发布了合成仿真代码和随机种子。

sents.en: These assets are accompanied by documentation describing the simulation procedure, dependencies, commands needed to reproduce the figures, and an appropriate license.
sents.zh: 这些资产附带文档，描述了仿真流程、依赖项、复现图表所需的命令，以及合适的许可证。

paragraphs.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets.
paragraphs.zh: 答案 [N/A] 表示该论文未发布新资产。

paragraphs.en: Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员应在提交材料中通过结构化模板说明数据集/代码/模型的详细信息。 这包括有关训练、许可证、局限性等方面的细节。

sents.en: Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates.
sents.zh: 研究人员应在提交材料中通过结构化模板说明数据集/代码/模型的详细信息。

sents.en: This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc.
sents.zh: 这包括有关训练、许可证、局限性等方面的细节。

paragraphs.en: The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used.
paragraphs.zh: 论文应讨论是否以及如何从其资产被使用的人们那里获得同意。

paragraphs.en: At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file.
paragraphs.zh: 在提交时，请记得对你的资产进行匿名化处理（如适用）。 你可以创建一个匿名化的 URL，或者附上一个匿名化的 zip 文件。

sents.en: At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable).
sents.zh: 在提交时，请记得对你的资产进行匿名化处理（如适用）。

sents.en: You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file.
sents.zh: 你可以创建一个匿名化的 URL，或者附上一个匿名化的 zip 文件。

paragraphs.en: Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects
paragraphs.zh: 众包与人类受试者研究

paragraphs.en: Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：对于众包实验和涉及人类受试者的研究，论文是否在适用的情况下包含了提供给参与者的完整指令文本及截图，以及报酬（如有）的详细信息？

paragraphs.en: Justification: The paper does not involve crowdsourcing or research with human subjects.
paragraphs.zh: 理由：该论文不涉及众包或以人类为对象的研究。

paragraphs.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects.
paragraphs.zh: 答案 [N/A] 表示该论文不涉及众包，也不涉及以人类为受试者的研究。

paragraphs.en: Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper.

paragraphs.en: According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector.
paragraphs.zh: 根据 NeurIPS 伦理准则，参与数据收集、整理或其他劳动的工作人员应获得不低于数据收集者所在国家最低工资标准的报酬。

paragraphs.en: Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained?
paragraphs.zh: 问题：论文是否描述了研究参与者可能承担的风险、这些风险是否已向受试者披露，以及是否获得了机构审查委员会（IRB）的批准（或基于您所在国家或机构要求的等效批准/审查）？

paragraphs.en: Justification: The paper does not involve human subjects research, so IRB approval or equivalent review is not applicable.
paragraphs.zh: 理由：本文不涉及人类受试者研究，因此不适用 IRB 批准或同等审查。

paragraphs.en: Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper.
paragraphs.zh: 根据开展研究所处的国家不同，任何涉及人类受试者的研究可能都需要获得伦理审查委员会（IRB）的批准（或同等审批）。 如果你已获得伦理审查委员会（IRB）的批准，应在论文中明确说明这一点。

paragraphs.en: For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review.
paragraphs.zh: 初次提交时，请勿包含任何会破坏匿名性（如适用）的信息，例如开展评审的机构。
